newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST -- BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST -- BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
-- Georgi Agafonov, former head of the private Slavyani bank, put in receivership last year, was elected deputy in the new parliament on the ticket of the Bulgarian Business Block.

-- Bulgaria's banking system has begun to stabilise after 14 commercial banks were put in receivership by the central bank in 1996 and banking control was strengthened. The country's banks posted a 157 billion levs net profit in 1996, up from 28 billion levs loss in the previous year, commercial banks' annual reports showed.
-- Bulgaria's judicial system contested a new bank insolvency bill, to be approved by the new parliament, which empowers the central bank to bankrupt banks.

-- The Executive dorector of the Sofarma pharmaceutical plant, Anton Petrov, was banned from travelling to France with the group of Bulgarian businessmen which accompanied President Petar Stoyanov last week.
-- The second round of mass privatisation is about to start.
-- Bulgaria's central bank is expected to cut further its main interest rate to 5.5 percent from the current 6.2 percent on the base of the yields of the last seven-day and 28-day T-bills auctions.
-- International Monetary Fund officials are optimistic about Bulgaria's reforms, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said after a visit to the IMF headquarters in Washington.
-- ABN Amro Bank is expected to participate in the management of the Bulgarian Biochim Bank with whom it signed a twinning agreement last year.
-- An IMF mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria in May to help set up a currency board system. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
